newsitem.title: PERU: Andean Pact meets to discuss Peru re-entry plan.
newsitem.headline: Andean Pact meets to discuss Peru re-entry plan.

text.p: Representatives of the Andean Pact met Tuesday to discuss Peru's plan for adhering to the group's common import tariff, part of the country's proposal for rejoining the regional trade group, officials said.
Sources at the pact's Board of Cartagena administrative entity said Peru, at a closed-door meeting Tuesday, had applied for a gradual return to the five-member pact over eight years.
Representatives of the member nations began meeting at 0930 local (1430 GMT) at the Board offices in Lima to discuss the Peruvian proposal.

The Andean Pact, comprised of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela, with Peru's membership suspended, decided in January at a meeting in Caracas to grant Peru until Tuesday to reincorporate itself to the group.
Peru decided in 1992 to temporarily leave the pact over disagreenment with its tariff policy after deciding it went against its internal free-market economic policies.
